definition: The fraction of predictions a model gets right. Misleading on imbalanced data: predicting the majority class always can score 99% while catching none of the rare events.
A nonlinear function (ReLU, sigmoid, GELU) applied to a neuron's output. Without it, a stack of linear layers collapses into one linear layer.
A mechanism where each token computes a weighted average over all other tokens, with weights derived from content similarity. The core of the Transformer architecture.
Area Under the ROC Curve: the probability that a random positive example scores higher than a random negative one. Use PR-AUC instead when the positive class is rare.
The algorithm that computes gradients through a network by applying the chain rule backwards from the loss. Makes gradient-based training of deep models tractable.
Training many models on bootstrap-resampled subsets of the data and averaging their predictions. Reduces variance; the basis of Random Forests.
The simplest legitimate model you must beat — the majority class, the mean, or plain logistic regression. A model without a baseline score is uninterpretable.
Normalizes each layer's activations across the mini-batch, stabilizing and speeding up training. Also acts as a mild regularizer.
The rule for updating belief in a hypothesis given evidence: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior. The mathematical engine behind everything from spam filters to imbalanced-data reasoning.
Error decomposes into bias (systematic wrongness from a too-simple model) and variance (sensitivity to the particular training sample). Tuning complexity trades one for the other.
Training models sequentially, each new one fitting the errors of the ensemble so far. Reduces bias; the basis of AdaBoost, XGBoost and LightGBM.
Resampling the data with replacement to estimate the variability of a statistic — the cheap way to put a confidence interval on a model metric.
Whether predicted probabilities mean what they say: among cases predicted 0.7, roughly 70% should be positive. Essential when probabilities drive decisions.
When one class vastly outnumbers another (fraud, defaults, disease). Accuracy becomes useless; resampling, class weights and PR-AUC take over.
Grouping data without labels. K-means is the workhorse; choosing the number of clusters is a modeling decision, not a fact you discover.
The 2×2 table of true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives. Every classification metric is arithmetic on these four cells.
Sliding a small learned filter across an image to produce feature maps. Exploits spatial locality and shares weights, making it vastly more parameter-efficient than dense layers on images.
A linear association measure between two numeric variables, from -1 to 1. Zero correlation does not imply independence, and correlation never implies causation.
The standard classification loss: the average negative log-probability the model assigns to the truth. Minimizing it is maximum likelihood.
Splitting data into k folds, training k times, each time holding out a different fold for evaluation. The honest way to estimate generalization — if done leakage-free.
The input distribution changing after deployment, silently degrading a model. Detected with distribution comparisons on live features; the reason models need monitoring.

Information from outside the training window sneaking into features — most catastrophically, anything recorded because of the outcome. The top cause of models that look brilliant and fail in production.
A model that partitions data with a hierarchy of yes/no questions chosen to maximize purity. Interpretable but prone to overfitting alone; powerful ensembled.
Compressing many features into fewer while preserving structure — PCA for variance, UMAP/t-SNE mostly for visualization. Helps models and humans both.
Training a small student model to match a large teacher's output distribution, transferring capability at a fraction of the serving cost.
Randomly zeroing a fraction of activations during training so no neuron can rely on a specific partner. Cheap, effective regularization for neural networks.
Halting training when validation loss stops improving. Simultaneously saves compute and prevents overfitting; nearly free, nearly always worth it.
A dense vector representation of an item (word, user, image) where geometric closeness encodes semantic similarity. The substrate of modern search and RAG.
Combining several models so their errors cancel. Bagging, boosting and stacking are the three families; almost every tabular competition winner is an ensemble.
One full pass of the training data through the model. Losses per epoch — train vs validation — are the primary training diagnostic.
The systematic first pass over a dataset: distributions, missingness, relationships, anomalies. Where hypotheses form and where most project-saving discoveries happen.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall. Punishes imbalance between them, unlike the arithmetic mean — use it when both error types matter.
Constructing informative inputs from raw data — ratios, aggregations, encodings, time lags. Still the highest-leverage skill on tabular problems.
Continuing training of a pretrained model on your task's data. Cheaper than training from scratch and usually better; LoRA made it affordable for LLMs.
Performance on data the model never saw — the only performance that matters. The train/validation gap is its early-warning system.
The vector of partial derivatives of a loss with respect to parameters — the direction of steepest increase. Training moves parameters the other way.
Sequentially adding small trees, each fitting the previous ensemble's residuals. The dominant family for tabular data.
Iteratively updating parameters against the gradient of the loss: theta ← theta − lr·∇L. Every deep learning optimizer is a variation on this one line.
The labels assumed correct for training and evaluation. Worth auditing — a noisy or leaked ground truth invalidates everything downstream.
A language model generating fluent, confident text that is factually wrong. Mitigated by grounding (RAG), citations and evaluation — never fully eliminated.
A setting chosen before training (learning rate, tree depth, k in k-fold) rather than learned from data. Tuned with validation, grids or Bayesian search.
The framework for deciding whether an observed effect is distinguishable from noise: null hypothesis, test statistic, p-value, error types.
Filling in missing values with estimates (mean, median, model-based). Always add a missing-indicator feature — missingness is often informative.
The reduction in entropy from knowing a variable's value — the split criterion of decision trees and a feature-ranking measure in its own right.
Using a trained model to predict on new data. Also the serving phase where latency, batching and cost engineering actually matter.
The interactive environment where analysis lives — great for exploration, dangerous as a delivery mechanism. Logic graduates from notebook to package.
Iteratively assigning points to the nearest of k centroids, then recentering. Fast and standard; requires choosing k and assumes roughly spherical clusters.
Computing similarities in a high-dimensional implicit feature space via kernel functions, letting linear methods learn nonlinear boundaries (SVMs).
The asymmetric measure of how one probability distribution differs from another — the quantity minimized (in disguise) whenever a model is trained.
The step size of gradient descent. Too small crawls; too large diverges; schedules and warmup manage the trade-off over training.
The probability of the observed data under a hypothesized model, viewed as a function of the model's parameters. Maximizing it is the classical path to fitting.
The raw, unnormalized scores a network outputs before softmax or sigmoid. Loss functions like cross-entropy consume logits for numerical stability.
The scalar a model minimizes — the definition of 'learning' for that model. Choose it to match the decision, not the convenience of the library.
Models that consume more than one modality — text plus images plus audio. Contrastive pretraining (CLIP) aligns their embedding spaces.
The amount of uncertainty about one variable removed by knowing another. Detects any dependency, not just linear ones; used for feature selection.
A classifier applying Bayes' theorem with an (incorrect but effective) assumption that features are independent given the class. Still a strong text baseline.
Stacked layers of linear transformations and nonlinear activations, trained by gradient descent. Universal approximator and the substrate of deep learning.
Rescaling features to comparable ranges (standardization, min-max). Matters for gradient-based models; unnecessary for trees.
Representing a categorical variable as binary indicator columns. Standard for linear models; trees prefer ordinal or target-aware encodings.
A point far from the bulk of the data. Sometimes an error to fix, sometimes the most important observation in the dataset — investigate before deleting.
Memorizing the training set at the expense of generalization — great train scores, weak validation scores. Controlled by regularization, more data or simpler models.
Principal Component Analysis: rotating data onto the directions of maximum variance, found as eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. Compression, decorrelation and visualization.
A single object chaining preprocessing and model so transforms are fit on training folds only. The structural defense against leakage.
Area under the Precision-Recall curve. The headline metric for imbalanced problems, where ROC-AUC flatters models that ignore the minority class.
Of the cases you flagged, the fraction that were truly positive. The cost asymmetry metric: high precision protects the people you act on.
Designing model inputs — instructions, examples, structure, constraints — to reliably get the behavior you want. The LLM-era skill of programming in prose.
The probability of observing data at least as extreme as yours if the null hypothesis were true. Not the probability the hypothesis is false.
A cut point dividing a distribution so that a fraction of the data lies below it — medians, quartiles, percentiles. Robust to outliers where means are not.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: fetch relevant documents, then have the LLM answer grounded in them. Up-to-date, attributable knowledge without retraining.
An ensemble of de-correlated decision trees fit on bootstrap samples, averaged. The strongest zero-tuning baseline for tabular data.
Of the truly positive cases, the fraction you caught. The coverage metric: high recall protects the people you miss.
Any constraint that trades a little training accuracy for generalization — L1/L2 penalties, dropout, early stopping, data augmentation.
Training an agent from reward signals through interaction rather than labeled examples. RLHF — its application to align LLMs — produced the assistant behavior of modern chat models.
True-positive rate against false-positive rate across all thresholds. AUC summarizes it; read it with the base rate in mind.
The fraction of target variance a regression explains, relative to predicting the mean. Comparisons need the same target and population — it is not a universal quality score.
Selecting a subset of data to represent a population. Random sampling underwrites nearly every statistical guarantee you rely on.
Converts a vector of raw scores into a probability distribution: exponentiate, normalize. The standard output layer of multi-class models and LLM token heads.
Learning a mapping from inputs to labels using labeled examples. The workhorse paradigm behind this site's capstone.
Mapping features to comparable ranges (z-score, min-max, log). Gradient-based models converge better; trees don't care.
The n-dimensional array — scalars, vectors, matrices and beyond — and the universal data container of PyTorch and TensorFlow.
The final, untouched holdout used once to estimate deployed performance. Touch it repeatedly and it silently becomes a second validation set.
Data ordered in time, where temporal leakage and autocorrelation break standard validation. Demands forward-chaining splits and lagged features.
Splitting text into model-consumable units (subwords via BPE). The bridge between human language and the embedding table.
The data a model fits directly. Everything else exists to measure what the fitting generalized.
Reusing a model pretrained on a large general task for your smaller specific one — initialize from the checkpoint, adapt the head, optionally fine-tune.
The architecture built entirely on attention — parallelizable, scalable, and the foundation of modern LLMs and vision models alike.
The model is too simple for the signal: training and validation scores are both poor. Remedy with capacity, features or training time — not regularization.
Learning structure from unlabeled data — clustering, dimensionality reduction, density estimation. Where EDA and representation learning live.
The holdout used during development to compare models and tune hyperparameters. It must be sacred: leak it and every comparison is corrupted.
The squared spread of a random variable around its mean — in models, the sensitivity of results to the particular training sample.
A store for embeddings with fast approximate nearest-neighbor search (HNSW, IVF). The retrieval engine of RAG systems.
SQL functions computed across a window of related rows (ROW_NUMBER, LAG, running sums) without collapsing rows. The workhorse of feature building from event data.
The engineered gradient boosting system — second-order objectives, sparsity-aware splits, regularized leaf weights. The default winner on tabular problems.
A value expressed in standard deviations from the mean. The standard yardstick for outliers and for comparing across differently-scaled features.
